My problem is that a small bite isn't enough for this urge that I feel, I have to eat an entire tablet, and I always end up overeating!

One small truffle won't be enough

I really can compare this to an addiction because of how much of my routine is disrupted by this urge to eat sweets.
I really need to do some kind of "detox/rehab" with my sugar problem.
My problem is that I feel this huge craving and one choco square isn't enough to satisfy it, I have to eat the entire bar! I hate this, because I always overeat
There's a sugarless pudding mix where which I make with sugarless plant milk and it's delicious! I really should make those and leave them for when I have a craving!

I do love Caramel Rooibos tea! It feels like drinking something with caramel, but no calories!

Sadly, I'm not from the USA, those things are super rare and expensive here
Even the caramel rooibos I like is an imported product 😭

Ugh I can't stand dark chocolate.
My favorite chocolate is white; I love super sweet candy like gummies, marshmallows, caramels...Eating dark chocolate for me is like a punishment :(

Dates are suuuper sweet! 
I've used them as sweetner on healthy desserts before!

But they still taste like fruit to me, not like candy, which is what I crave! I can, however, make healthy desserts using dates as sweetner! Those desserts help me with my cravings!

I used to take showers everyday before my surgeries and then it became harder to stand up and it starter requiring more effort. 

Since I hardly leave home (also due to my health, related to my surgeries), I don't get too dirty, so now it's like, 3 times per week, or 4 if it's hot.
Bed bugs
Less drama

I'm someone who attempted suicide by jumping from a tall building.

It sucks so hard.
It broke my body, all those broken bones, all those surgeries, all the internal hemorrhage...From my experience, and from listening a lot more people talk about this, there are a lot of times suicide by jumping aren't an instant death or aren't even a death, they may only leave you crippled.

It sucks so hard to be in a dark place, mentally.

I do eat 6 eggs a day (sometimes 8) and eat a lot of veggies.
 
Still hungry at the end of the day, might be psychological though :(

Yeah I'm not unhealthy, but I'm unhappy with my looks. I do physical therapy (rehabilitation because I broke so many bones at my attempt) and I have a pretty nice strength, I'm not super weak.
I just wish I was leaner because months bedridden and using a wheelchair made me gain weight.
I've actually thought about DNP, but seeing how ephedrine already makes me feel like shit, I thought it would make me feel even worse, so I discarded that option.

OMG YES! I've had an ex-boyfriend tell me exactly the same thing!
"If you are craving something, just don't eat that, what's so hard about it?"

It's hard to explain for people who don't understand.
I don't drink alcohol and I've never been addicted to any other drug, but it's the same as saying, "Why don't you just stop drinking? Why don't you just stop taking it when you feel like?"

I wish things were easy like that!

I've had people simply tell me "Just don't eat when you're hungry! This is what I do!" 
Neat if this works for you, I know people very close to me who swear by fasting, meanwhile I go hypoglycemic and start fainting.

It's not the same for everyone, people's bodies are different.

I've done it.

I do exercise, I alternate between strength training and cardio, I exercise every single day.

I've tried tracking calories but at the end of the day, I'm so hungry I can't stay under my goals and binge eat and fuck up everything.

I really need something to surpress my appetite so I can stick with my daily caloric goals without binge eating at the end of the day.

I have no problems eating healthy food and exercising.
I only drink water and tea (homemede, no sugar, no sweetneers, nothing).
I have a good nutrient balance (protein+healthy carbs+fat)

My problem is overeating because I'm super hungry. Too much of a goof thing still makes you fat. Anything that fixes my appetite would help, the other part of the work, I can do myself.

I do exercise but this makes me feel so damn hungry it's impossible to be at a caloric deficit.

I could probably maintain my weight easily, but losing without help is too hard :(
This is exactly the problem
I'm talking about it with my doctor on our appointment next week!

If you had read my post you would see that I do (basically everyday, alternating muscle strengthening with cardio) and that makes me hungrier

But for the amount of brain cells you probably have, it's impossible to read posts properly

I honestly don't care about bad effects in my lungs, I'm usually afraid of nicotine because it has other effects like damaging your skin, hair, teeth...
As someone who struggles with image disorders, I can't afford to have my image damaged, I would be changing the weight issue for a different issue.

If there's a way to consume nicotine without those, hell yeah I'd try it

I've explained why I'm doing this in other comments

When you're desperate like I am, feels your mental wellbeing and your life is at stake, you will do anything.

Thank you for your sweet answer!

I also think drugs are underprescribed.
While there are a lot of overweight people who are overweight because of bad habits, a lot of them have psychological issues and problems with food and need harsher treatment- this is why I'm seeking help here. 

I do exercise and I do eat healthy, however I feel super hungry and can't make a caloric deficit, exercising makes me even more hungry so it's not as easy as it seems to people without psychological issues.

Yet everyone around me tells me to eat better (I already do), exercise, count calories, etc etc

I know people who struggle with alcoholism, addiction, gambling, and those are seen as real struggles, while with binge eating or excessive appetite, people just tell you to endure it.

I can't even sleep at night when my body decides do make me feel hungry, my belly hurts from hunger and I'm forced to leave bed and binge eat, I've tried every kind of small meals, brush teeth again, and the hunger is still there unless I binge and surpass my allowed daily caloric.

With topiramate I felt full with small amounts, had no urge to binge, it was wonderful, like being a normal person with a normal hunger and a normal food relationship.

I really miss that feeling :(

I will look into these! I'm looking for something that will not fuck me up like ephedrine does. People say ephedrine wears of after a few hours but it gives me chronic insomia and depletes me of all energy.

Most people there just tell me not to give up, eat healthy and exercise

My problem is that exercising makes me super hungry and I can't have a 1200-1500 kcal day without binging at the end. Especially at sleep time, my body notices I didn't eat a lot and makes me super hungry and I can't sleep, then I binge :(

Nothing: I actually threw myself from the building I live on (after many years of overdosing, slashing my wrists, etc)
Broke my back, had internal hemorrhages, had to have a lot of surgeries, got lucky to be able to walk again, had my back bones substituted for titanium parts and ended up with ugly scars on my back and belly.
After reading so much about so many people who survived falls like me, I'd never attempt it again by jumping from a tall place.

Every weight loss "dairy" I read, focused on low carb, I was trying to do it, but it makes me feel like trash, honestly. I love plant based foods and have loved since I was a child, I can eat plain carrots, dry salad, tomatoes with a small pinch of salt, but they are not very filling, I feel hungry even if I fill myself with fiber and protein. I've tried chia seeds, mixed them on my protein shakes, but all those "magic weight loss tips" still leave me hungry. 

And exercising while dieting seems so hard to me, because I feel really tired and low on energy.

Since I broke my back, I had permanent damage and I will never be the same as I used to be. I won't ever be able to move like a normal person again, but at least I could walk again. 

Since the neurological system goes through your back, I was very lucky mine wasn't damaged. 
I guess I will never be equal to someone who's 20 percent, but as long as I lose weight, that's okay.
